papers.title: Utility of Rt epidemic trend categories for influenza surveillance: alignment with observed emergency department trends across two influenza seasons in the United States
papers.abstract: CDC has estimated the time-varying reproduction number (Rt) for influenza in the United States since 2023, translating the posterior probability that Rt exceeds one, P(R_t>1), into epidemic trend categories (growing, likely growing, not changing, likely declining, declining). If Rt reliably indicates infection dynamics, growing or declining trends should precede corresponding changes in influenza-related emergency department (ED) visits, accounting for the lag between infection and care-seeking. However, because these categories reflect confidence in the direction of change rather than magnitude, their alignment with the corresponding trends ED activity measures is unclear. We compared weekly Rt epidemic trend categories to observed ED trends from the National Syndromic Surveillance Program across the 2024/2025 and 2025/2026 influenza seasons, using three thresholds to define observed trends at different magnitudes ([≥]0.1% difference, [≥]0.5% difference, [≥]5% relative change between consecutive weeks), comparing Rt trends to observed trends the following week. We assessed categorical alignment and calibration between P(R_t>1) and observed trends. Alignment was moderate overall, strongest for growing and declining categories under the 5% relative change threshold (61% aligned) and weakest under the 0.5% difference threshold (38.2% aligned); calibration was similarly best under the 5% relative change threshold. Misalignment concentrated around epidemic inflection points and periods of low influenza activity. Rt epidemic trend categories showed moderate, threshold-dependent alignment with observed ED activity, reflecting a combination of real-time model error and misalignment between direction-based and magnitude-based surveillance metrics. Defining categories based on Rt magnitude could improve correspondence with size-based change indicators and strengthen their utility for real-time monitoring.

papers.title: From telling to receiving: the disclosure-and-services cascade after childhood sexual abuse across 15 low- and middle-income countries
papers.abstract: Most children who experience sexual abuse in low- and middle-income countries never receive formal help, but few studies have followed survivors through the steps from telling someone to receiving services. In this pooled cross-sectional analysis, we combined 15 nationally representative Violence Against Children and Youth Surveys (VACS) fielded between 2013 and 2024 in sub-Saharan Africa, Latin America, and Eastern Europe to describe this disclosure-and-services cascade and the factors associated with each step. The analytic sample comprised 3,608 respondents aged 18-24 years who reported sexual abuse before age 18 (2,852 female, 756 male). We estimated survey-weighted proportions for four steps: told anyone, knew where to seek formal help, sought help (among those who knew), and received help (among those who sought it). Design-based logistic regression with country fixed effects estimated adjusted odds ratios (aORs) for individual, family, and community factors. Overall, 47.1% (95% confidence interval [CI] 44.4-49.7) of survivors had told anyone and 34.8% (32.2-37.5) knew where to seek formal help. Of those who knew (n = 1,208), 24.8% (20.9-29.1) sought help, and of those who sought help (n = 339), 81.9% (75.9-86.7) received it. In total, 7.0% (5.7-8.5) of survivors received formal help; this proportion ranged from 0.9% to 26.3% across countries. Compared with male survivors, female survivors were more likely to tell anyone (aOR 2.30, 95% CI 1.73-3.05) and less likely to know where to seek help (aOR 0.68, 0.50-0.93); among survivors who knew where to go, female survivors were more likely to seek help (aOR 2.66, 1.39-5.09). Knowing where to seek help was more likely with older age, more schooling, and a living mother. Survivors who had ever married or cohabited were less likely to have told anyone (aOR 0.75, 0.58-0.96). No factor other than sex was associated with seeking help among those who knew where to go. Most survivors are lost before they reach a service: two in three do not know where to go, and three in four of those who know ultimately do not seek help. Once survivors seek help, most receive it. Interventions should make services known to young people, particularly those with less schooling, and address the barriers that keep survivors, especially young men, from using services they know about.

papers.title: Knowledge, attitudes and behaviours related to tick awareness and prevention among users of urban green spaces: insights from stakeholder focus groups
papers.abstract: Abstract Background: Ticks in the UK can transmit pathogens that lead to diseases in humans, including Lyme disease and tick-borne encephalitis. Expanding tick populations and increasing human use of urban green spaces may elevate exposure risk. Public health advice exists, but little is known about how this guidance is understood and applied by users of urban environments. Methods: Four stakeholder focus groups were conducted with professionals involved in tick fieldwork in urban green spaces. Discussions explored interactions with the public, perceived awareness, behaviours, and views on communication. Data were analysed thematically using an approach informed by the Framework Method. Results: Stakeholders reported substantial variation in public awareness of ticks, influenced by prior exposure to rural environments and local knowledge. Misinformation, particularly around tick removal, was common. Signage was rarely observed in urban green spaces, and views on its effectiveness were mixed. Participants emphasised the need to balance risk communication with reassurance and highlighted the importance of age-appropriate education. Conclusions: Insights from stakeholders underline the importance of targeted, context specific public health messaging in urban settings. Priorities include identifying groups with lower awareness, addressing misinformation, designing balanced communication materials, evaluating the effectiveness of signage, and integrating education for children and families.

papers.title: Applying Diagnostic Network Optimisation analysis to inform the introduction of G6PD testing into Indonesia for improved treatment of relapsing malaria
papers.abstract: Background: Radical cure for P. vivax and P. ovale malaria using 8-aminoquinoline drugs primaquine or tafenoquine can prevent relapse, but requires glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) screening due to the risk of haemolysis in G6PD-deficient individuals. This study aimed to provide an evidence-based framework to inform the optimal allocation and referral networks for G6PD testing devices in Indonesia. Methods: A diagnostic network optimisation (DNO) analysis using OptiDx was conducted across eight districts in Sumba, North Sumatra, and Central Java, representing high-, moderate-, and low-transmission settings. The maximum annual number of malaria cases from surveillance data between 2019 and 2022 was used as a proxy for testing demand. In baseline scenario, all public health facilities were equipped with G6PD testing devices. In referral scenario, devices were allocated only to selected facilities, with a maximum sample transport distance of 15 kilometres and sample delivery scheduled three times per week. Model outputs were reviewed with the National Malaria Control Programme (NMCP) to identify the optimal scenario, considering factors including implementation cost and accessibility. Results: Equipping 39% (30/76) of facilities in Sumba with G6PD testing devices could reduce total costs by nearly 30% in the first year and approximately 20% in subsequent years compared with the baseline, although the average referral distance increased from 4.48 kilometres to 9.8 kilometres. In North Sumatra, deploying 15 of 68 devices (19%) could reduce total costs by almost 60% in the first year and approximately 15% thereafter. Two health facilities (Puskesmas Padewatu in Sumba and Abdul Manan Hospital in North Sumatra) could experience workload increase exceeding 400 hours annually as referral facilities. In Purworejo, a single device placed at Puskesmas Mranti could enable on-site diagnosis for 56% of patients. Interpretation: The findings demonstrated that DNO can identify cost-efficient and equitable G6PD testing strategies to support safe radical cure and accelerate malaria elimination.

papers.title: Validation of the PACER-PT: a measure of health-relevant perceptions of gentrification-related neighbourhood change
papers.abstract: Objective: Urban neighbourhoods across Europe are rapidly transforming through gentrification, with Portuguese cities particularly affected. Although the health impacts of these changes are increasingly recognised, validated instruments to assess perceptions of neighbourhood change remain scarce. This study adapted and validated a Portuguese version of the Perceptions About Change in Environment and Residents (PACER-PT) scale. Methods: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among 255 adults living for >=5yrs in the Lisbon and Porto Metropolitan Areas. PACER was translated and culturally adapted to create PACER-PT. We evaluated psychometric properties using exploratory factor analysis (EFA), internal consistency, and convergent and criterion validity. Results: EFA identified a three-factor structure explaining 47.5% of the variance: Built, social and economic changes, Positive attitude towards neighbourhood changes, and Displacement concerns and neighbourhood disruption. Internal consistency was acceptable (Cronbach s alpha=0.70-0.78). Convergent/criterion validity were supported by significant associations with amount and pace of change, self-rated health, and quality of life. Younger and wealthier participants and those with greater residential satisfaction reported more favourable perceptions. Conclusions: PACER-PT demonstrated it is a valid instrument for assessing gentrification-related neighbourhood changes in Portugal.

papers.title: The impact of warning labels versus traffic light labels on food choice and negative emotional responses: two randomised controlled trials among UK adult populations with and without an eating disorder
papers.abstract: Background In the UK, front-of-pack traffic light labels (TLL) are implemented voluntarily. The UK Government are considering alternative FOP approaches, such as nutrient warning labels (WL). However, the effects and potential harm of TLL versus WL in UK consumers are unclear. We compared the effects of WL, TLL, and no label on unhealthy food item selection and negative affect among UK adults with and without an eating disorder (ED). Methods We conducted two online randomised controlled trials. In Study 1, 924 UK adults without an ED diagnosis were randomly assigned (1:1:1) to a WL, TLL, or no labels condition and completed a food-choice task. In Study 2, 240 UK adults with an ED diagnosis completed a baseline no-label food choice task and were subsequently randomly assigned (1:1:1) to WL, TLL, or no labels for a follow-up food choice task. The primary outcome was the number of task-specific unhealthy food items selected. Negative affect before and after food choice tasks was measured as a secondary outcome. Findings In Study 1 (data collected 02/25 - 04/25), unhealthy food selection differed by condition (p = .013). Of five products selected, WL participants selected 0.20 fewer unhealthy items than TLL participants (8.0%; p = .038) and 0.28 fewer than controls (10.7%; p = .004). In Study 2 (data collected 11/25 - 02/26), unhealthy selection decreased by 0.39 items with WL (17.7%; p = .015), 0.13 with TLL (5.3%, p = .286), and 0.00 with no labels. The reduction was greater with WL than with no labels (p = .029). Label condition did not differentially affect task-related negative affect in either study (Study 1, p = .757; Study 2, p = .448). Interpretation WL tended to be associated with lower unhealthy food selection compared to TLL in UK adults. There was minimal evidence that WL or TLL caused negative emotional responses. Funding This research was funded by the National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) Oxford Health BRC. The views expressed are those of the author(s) and not necessarily those of the NIHR or the Department of Health and Social Care. Registration ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07339969

papers.title: Oral rehydration salts and zinc for childhood diarrhoea in Bangladesh, 2019 and 2025: coverage, wealth inequality and reported source of care
papers.abstract: Background: Diarrhoea remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality among children under five. WHO and UNICEF recommend oral rehydration salts (ORS) alongside 10 to 14 days of zinc supplementation. However, national progress in combined treatment coverage and its socioeconomic and care-related inequalities remains insufficiently understood in Bangladesh. We assessed combined coverage, wealth inequality and differences by reported source of care. Methods: We analysed children under five with caregiver-reported diarrhoea in the 2019 (n=1,589) and 2025 (n=1,634) Multiple Indicator Cluster Surveys (MICS). We estimated combined coverage using design-based methods, wealth inequality using slope indices, and associations with source of care using pooled adjusted prevalence ratios (aPR). Demographic and Health Survey (DHS) estimates provided an external comparison. Results: Combined ORS and zinc coverage increased from 35.0% (95% CI 32.3 to 37.7) in 2019 to 42.9% (40.1 to 45.8) in 2025. In 2025, ORS and zinc coverage were 75.8% and 51.9%, respectively. The 2025 estimate agreed with DHS 2022, whereas MICS 2019 was below DHS 2017-18. Wealth inequality persisted in 2025 (slope index 13.0 percentage points, 3.4 to 22.6). Adjustment attenuated the pooled slope index from 11.8 to 6.5 points (-1.7 to 14.6). Coverage was lower with pharmacy-only than public care (aPR 0.59, 0.53 to 0.66) and with no care reported (0.14, 0.11 to 0.18). Children with no care reported accounted for 43.7% of children without combined treatment in 2025. Conclusions: Combined coverage increased, although the apparent progress may be overstated by the lower MICS 2019 estimate relative to DHS. Zinc remained the larger treatment gap, while one in four children received no ORS. Reported sources of care require cautious interpretation.

papers.title: Serotype-structured force of infection for optimizing dengue vaccine trial design
papers.abstract: Dengue fever, transmitted primarily by Aedes aegypti, remains a major global public health threat, causing an estimated 390 million infections annually. Designing efficient dengue vaccine efficacy trials in endemic regions is challenging because transmission intensity varies across space and time, baseline population immunity is heterogeneous, and endpoint accrual depends strongly on the local force of infection (FoI). We developed a simulation framework for trial planning in endemic settings that links FoI to age-specific seroprevalence through a catalytic model and then translates FoI into symptomatic endpoint incidence for randomized controlled trial simulations. Across a range of FoI scenarios representing low-to-high endemic transmission, we evaluated sample size requirements, follow-up duration, and expected power under alternative vaccine efficacy assumptions. In high-transmission settings, the framework indicates that trials enrolling 5,000-10,000 participants per arm can achieve at least 80% power within 12-24 months of follow-up under plausible symptomatic detection assumptions. Sensitivity analyses demonstrate that feasibility thresholds are most sensitive to FoI and the symptomatic fraction, highlighting the importance of site selection and surveillance intensity. Overall, the proposed FoI-based approach provides practical guidance for dengue trial design, including sample size determination, follow-up planning, and the identification of epidemiological conditions under which vaccine evaluation is most efficient in endemic settings.

papers.title: Maternal mortality risk among Black women in Brazil: a nationwide spatial consensus approach
papers.abstract: Although preventable, maternal mortality remains a global challenge. Its burden is disproportionately concentrated in low- and middle-income settings. Substantial subnational geographical variations also persist within countries, driven by underlying socioeconomic disparities and unequal access to quality healthcare services. Here we propose a spatial consensus framework combining frequentist and Bayesian models to overcome variance instability in small-area estimates, mapping maternal mortality risk among Black women in Brazil to guide equitable public health interventions. Using nationwide surveillance data (2019 - 2024), we applied a spatial Poisson probability model to detect high-rate clusters of maternal mortality among Black women. Concurrently, Bayesian hierarchical spatial models were fitted to smooth small-area rates and stabilise variance. Results from both approaches were integrated into a five-level risk typology to categorize Brazilian municipalities. National aggregate reductions in Brazilian maternal mortality mask profound, spatially concentrated racial inequities. The spatial classification of risk scenarios identified 13 municipalities with Confirmed Critical Risk, 28 municipalities with Persistent Regional Risk, 12 municipalities with a Local Excess Alert, and 4 exhibiting Epidemiological Silence. The vast majority remained at the Expected Risk Level. The proposed spatial consensus framework translates complex spatio-temporal modelling into an operational typology for surveillance systems. This approach bridges the gap between spatial analytics and public health decision-making, providing a replicable tool to address structural racial disparities in maternal health within decentralised health systems.

papers.title: Chronic health conditions, multimorbidity and subsequent economic inactivity in three British birth cohorts
papers.abstract: Background. Economic inactivity due to ill-health has been rising in the United Kingdom. Chronic health conditions make up most of the burden of poor health, and frequently co-occur, yet the impact of multimorbidity on economic inactivity remains underexplored. Methods. Data was from three British birth cohorts (born in 1946, 1958 and 1970). Psychological distress, chronic back pain and cardiometabolic disease were assessed in participants' thirties and forties, and economic inactivity one to two decades later. Modified Poisson regression models with robust standard errors estimated associations between health and inactivity, accounting for economic activity at baseline and several socioeconomic and demographic confounders. We tested for multiplicative and additive interaction between condition pairs. Results. The prevalence of all three health conditions increased with age. Each was associated with a higher risk of later economic inactivity in fully adjusted models. Psychological distress was the strongest and most consistent predictor across cohorts (RR = 1.22 (95% CI 0.90-1.64) to 1.99 (95% CI 1.67-2.38)). Comorbidity was common; more than 10% of participants experienced two or more conditions in their forties. Risk of economic inactivity increased with multimorbidity. However, we found little evidence that risk for comorbidity exceeded the sum of individual conditions on either the multiplicative or additive scales. Conclusions. Common chronic conditions in adulthood, particularly when comorbid, are associated with a substantially higher risk of economic inactivity across decades-long time horizons. This association has persisted over time and across policy contexts.

papers.title: Higher Nocturnal Temperatures Shorten and Worsen Sleep with No Clear Evidence of Short-Term Compensatory Patterns
papers.abstract: Background & Objectives Rising nighttime temperatures menace sleep, yet evidence from large longitudinal studies combining objective and subjective sleep measures remains limited. Here, we therefore examined associations of nocturnal air and wet-bulb temperature with seven sleep parameters, including possible delayed effects. Methods We analysed wearable-derived and subjective sleep data from 326 home-care workers (270 women) in Switzerland between June and Early October 2025, resulting in 14,290 participant-nights. Nocturnal air temperature and humidity data were obtained from the dense MeteoSwiss monitoring network (mean distance from participants' homes, 8.6 km). Bayesian multilevel models estimated nonlinear same-night within-person and between-person associations, while exploratory lag models examined whether associations with nocturnal temperature were also evident for exposures one and two nights earlier. Results Sleep maintenance efficiency, the primary outcome, showed no meaningful association with nocturnal air temperature. In contrast, warmer-than-usual nights were associated with shorter total sleep time and poorer subjective sleep quality. Compared with a participant's usual exposure, total sleep time was 13.3 min shorter at +5C, while subjective sleep-quality scores worsened by 1.2 points. At +5C, the probability of sleeping less than 7 h was 10.6 percentage points higher than at -4C relative to a participant's usual exposure. Changes in sleep-stage percentages and recovery index were very small. Wet-bulb results were broadly comparable while exploratory lag analyses provided little evidence of consistent delayed effects. Conclusions Higher nocturnal ambient temperatures were associated with shorter and poorer sleep, with no evidence of short-term compensatory patterns. The results thus underline that sleep disturbances may represent an important pathway linking warming nights to human health.

papers.title: Longitudinal Associations of Cigarette Smoking, Smoking Intensity, and Smoking TrajectoriesWith Emergency Room Utilization Among U.S. Adults
papers.abstract: Background: Tobacco smoking is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in the United States, yet its longitudinal association with emergency room (ER) utilization remains understudied. We examined whether cigarette smoking, smoking intensity, and smoking trajectories were associated with subsequent ER use. Methods: We analyzed adult respondents from Waves 1-6 of the Population Assessment of Tobacco and Health Study. Wave 1-3 smoking status, intensity, and cigarettes/day were examined in relation to next-wave ER outcomes. Logistic generalized estimating equation models were used for any ER visit and frequent ER use (>=2 visits), and negative binomial models were used for ER visit count. Trajectory analyses examined Wave 1-5 smoking patterns and Wave 6 ER outcomes, with Wave 1-4 to Wave 5 as sensitivity analysis. Marginal structural models (with IPW) and propensity score matching were used to strengthen causal interpretation. Models adjusted for demographics, insurance, self-rated health, and baseline ER use. Survey weights with balanced repeated replication and Fay's adjustment were used. Results: In adjusted GEE models, current smoking was associated with higher subsequent ER utilization, including any ER visit (OR 1.128, 95% CI [1.068-1.191]), frequent ER use (OR 1.275, 95% CI [1.185-1.372]), and ER visit count (RR 1.264, 95% CI [1.160-1.377]; all p =20 cigarettes/day showed stronger associations with any ER visit (OR 1.231, 95% CI [1.127-1.345]), frequent ER use (OR 1.447, 95% CI [1.293-1.618]), and ER visit count (RR 1.368, 95% CI [1.245-1.504]; all p<0.001). Each additional cigarette/day was also associated with higher ER utilization (OR/RR range, 1.007-1.011; all p<0.001). Findings were consistent in marginal structural models and propensity score matched analyses. In trajectory analyses, new/intermittent and persistent smokers had significantly higher ER utilization, while former/intermittent smokers and sustained quitters did not differ from non-smokers, suggesting that this harmful association was eliminated by smoking cessation. Conclusions: Smoking, heavier intensity, and persistent or emerging smoking patterns were associated with higher subsequent ER utilization, while smoking cessation reduces ER risk to the same level as non-smokers. This supports smoking prevention and cessation as strategies to reduce acute healthcare burden.

papers.title: Constructing expert models of adolescent vaping behaviour: A mental models study
papers.abstract: Research on vaping prevention messages has predominantly examined adolescents perceptions of and responses and the research exploring how experts perspectives is limited. Expert knowledge is crucial for conceptualising the risk phenomenon and its key causal mechanisms, uncertainties, and issues that are relevant to address in evidence-based communication strategies. This study therefore explored how professionals and experts conceptualise and understand adolescent vaping behaviour, including its perceived causes and drivers. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with a purposive sample of 12 experts from medical research, addiction science, public health prevention, and adolescent-oriented practice in Norway. Data collection and analysis were informed by the mental models approach to risk communication. The analysis identified an expert-derived mental model/influence diagram of adolescent vaping behaviour. Across expert domains, vaping was understood as a multifactorial phenomenon emerging from interacting biological, psychological, and social factors operating across multiple system levels. The first theme describes vaping initiation as a socially embedded and often intermittent practice shaped by identity development, peer belonging, and low perceived harm. The second theme captures how vaping is enabled, sustained, and legitimised through interacting drivers operating across social, structural, commercial, and regulatory contexts. The third theme focuses on reinforcement processes, whereby nicotine dependence and emotional coping mechanisms contribute to more sustained use. According to these expert accounts, adolescent vaping is sustained and legitimised through broader processes of normalisation operating across multiple societal levels. The expert perspectives identified in this study suggest that comparative risk framings of e-cigarettes as less harmful than cigarettes, and the social functions of vaping within adolescent peer cultures, may be important considerations in the development of risk communication targeting adolescents.

papers.title: Extending Problem and Solution Trees: A Participatory Method for Community Partnership Development
papers.abstract: BackgroundProblem and solution trees (PASTs) are a participatory method for understanding complex environmental and systemic health problems and incorporating community input in appropriate solutions. While PASTs have been applied in international contexts to examine critical health concerns (e.g., hand-washing behaviors and malnutrition), their use in the United States (US) is limited. ObjectivesTogether with a Project Advisory Board (PAB), identify barriers to DASH (Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension) eating plan adoption and co-develop actionable solutions to low adherence for a historically marginalized community in the U.S. MethodsPASTs are visual tools. Over virtual and in-person meetings, we constructed and refined five distinct trees to address each core barrier to DASH adherence. We made real-time edits to trees in PowerPoint and engaged in group discussion to reach consensus on barriers and solutions. Supporting material included a project workbook distributed to the PAB. Meetings were audio-recorded, and transcripts were reviewed following each meeting to ensure the accuracy of each tree. The PAST method aided collaboration with the PAB by allowing members to identify additional barriers and refine the trees based on their knowledge and experience. PASTs additionally supported the community-engaged partnership by identifying the interconnectedness of core problems (i.e., limited supply of healthy foods and preference for salty foods). ConclusionsPASTs showed their relevance as tools for community-engaged research and responsive program planning. Challenges in creating and presenting intricate trees via online format highlight considerations for virtual facilitation and real-time documentation. Adaptations to the method are described for future use.

papers.title: The Story of Shukuru - a film to enhance knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding schistosomiasis and related elimination interventions in Pemba, Tanzania.
papers.abstract: BackgroundSchistosomiasis is a neglected tropical disease affecting individuals in 79 countries, primarily in sub-Saharan Africa. The World Health Organization recommends the treatment, snail control, and behavior change interventions to decrease prevalence, but culturally tailored interventions remain rare. Here we aim to determine the impact of an educational film on schistosomiasis-related knowledge, attitudes, and practices among schoolchildren and adults in Pemba, Tanzania. Methodology/Principal FindingsFrom November 2023 to February 2024, a survey was conducted among adult community members in 20 administrative areas in Pemba on their preferences for a planned film about schistosomiasis. The film was produced in March 2024 based on these suggestions and filmed in Pemba. In July 2024, a pretest-posttest study in ten administrative areas assessed the films impact on schistosomiasis-related knowledge, attitudes, and willingness to change behavior among children and adults. Binomial generalized linear mixed-effects models estimated changes in knowledge and attitudes before versus after viewing. Of 882 participants surveyed in 2023/24, 810 (91.8%) were willing to watch a film about schistosomiasis, most commonly on TV (545, 67.3%). The impact study included 195 children and 195 adults. The odds of a correct knowledge answer were 39% higher after viewing (OR 1.39, 95% CI 1.29-1.50, p<0.001), and the odds of a positive attitude were 77% higher (OR 1.77, 95% CI 1.47-2.12, p<0.001). Before the film, 71.9% (200/278) of participants used natural water bodies for daily activities, and 72.5% (145/200) of these never used protective clothing. Afterward, 88.2% (240/272) reported being likely to avoid water bodies and 54.4% (148/272) likely to use protective clothing. Conclusions/SignificanceAn educational film developed from community input and filmed locally increased knowledge and attitudes among children and adults and fostered willingness to adopt self-protective behaviors. However, willingness alone is insufficient without infrastructure (e.g., wells, tap water) to change behavior. Therefore, such investments remain essential for schistosomiasis elimination. Author SummarySchistosomiasis is a disease caused by parasitic worms that live in open freshwater bodies, and it affects people in many countries, most heavily in sub-Saharan Africa. People become infected through everyday contact with contaminated water, such as swimming, washing, or farming. The World Health Organization recommends treatment, snail control and behavior change to reduce the disease, but most educational efforts are not tailored to local culture. We worked with communities on the island of Pemba, Tanzania, to create an educational film about schistosomiasis, shaped by residents own ideas about what such a film should look like and where they would watch it. We then tested whether the film changed peoples knowledge, attitudes, and stated intentions around water contact, comparing childrens and adults responses before and after watching. Knowledge and positive attitudes both improved after viewing, and many participants said they intended to avoid risky water contact and use protective items such as rubber boots. However, good intentions are not enough on their own: without safer alternatives like wells or tap water stations, people may have no real choice but to keep using open water bodies. Eliminating schistosomiasis will require investment in this kind of infrastructure alongside education.

papers.title: Assessing HIV vulnerability among young women in South Africa: A comparison of three risk assessment tools
papers.abstract: BackgroundYoung women in sub-Saharan Africa remain disproportionately affected by HIV. However, self-perceived HIV risk may not align with reported sexual behaviors or other dimensions of risk. Behavioral measures, such as the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART), may capture risk-taking propensity not reflected in conventional self-report measures. We compared self-perceived HIV risk, behavior-based HIV risk, and behavioral risk-taking propensity among young women in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. MethodsWe conducted a cross-sectional survey between July and November 2025 among self-reported HIV-negative women aged 18-30 years in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. We assessed self-perceived HIV risk using the Perceived Risk of HIV Scale (PRHS), behavior-based HIV risk using the Vaginal and Oral Interventions to Control the Epidemic (VOICE) Risk Score, and behavioral risk-taking propensity using the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART). Spearmans rank correlation coefficients were used to examine correlations between the three measures. ResultsAmong 250 participants, median age was 22 years (IQR 20-25), all identified as Black, and 53.6% were attending school or college. Overall, 42.0% were classified as high risk by VOICE, 6.0% by PRHS, and 33.1% of participants with complete BART data were in the highest tertile of risk-taking propensity. Mean age differed across VOICE categories (p = 0.036), but not PRHS (p = 0.111) or BART categories (p = 0.698). PRHS categories were associated with anal intercourse, oral intercourse, consistent condom use, ever having sold sex, and age-disparate partnerships (all p 0.05). ConclusionsThese findings highlight the importance of distinguishing between reported HIV risk behaviours, perceived HIV risk, and behavioural risk-taking propensity when assessing HIV vulnerability among young women. For HIV prevention programmes, reliance on a single measure may not adequately capture the different dimensions of vulnerability. Integrating behavioural assessments with discussions of perceived risk and individual circumstances may help inform more responsive, person-centred HIV prevention services, including PrEP counselling. Further research is needed to establish how these measures can best complement one another in prevention service delivery.

papers.title: Integrating 16S and 18S sequencing reveals coupled prokaryotic and eukaryotic relationships in drinking water biofilms
papers.abstract: Drinking water biofilms host diverse communities spanning all realms of life. However, despite the known interactions between opportunistic pathogens and microbial eukaryotes such as amoebae, most studies focus only on the prokaryotic populations in these systems. As a result, the degree to which microbial eukaryotes shape biofilm communities and the persistence of opportunistic waterborne pathogens, such as Legionella spp. is still largely unknown. Here we leveraged a set of 128 non-disinfected drinking water shower hose biofilms collected across Switzerland to characterize both communities and quantify eukaryotes role in shaping prokaryotic communities and Legionella persistence. We found both communities to present a conserved set of core taxa dominated by oligotrophic bacterial families and amoebae. The prevalence of taxa was mainly driven by the phylogenetic diversity among their sequence variants rather than their number alone. We detected prokaryotic and eukaryotic communities to show similar patterns in their richness and composition, influencing each other more than abiotic building-level factors. Legionellaceae bacteria were detected in 82% of samples presenting a diversity extending known reference species and no clear dominant taxa. Legionellaceae richness did not correlate with the richness of known amoebal hosts, but rather other amoebae, indicating that eukaryotic taxa relevant for Legionella persistence extend beyond the classically described hosts. These findings highlight the importance of integrating the eukaryotic communities to understand the microbial ecology in drinking water biofilms and recognize the conditions which allow opportunistic waterborne pathogens such as Legionella to persist.

papers.title: Decomposing the Caesarean section trend in Bangladesh (2012-2025): A multivariate Linear Probability Model analysis
papers.abstract: BackgroundWhile Caesarean section is a life-saving intervention when medically indicated, the World Health Organization recommends an optimal population-level rate of 10% to 15% to prevent iatrogenic morbidities. In Bangladesh, however, rapid clinical integration within a commercialized, dual-practice healthcare architecture has coincided with an unprecedented escalation in surgical deliveries. Because standard cross-sectional models cannot algebraically separate population shifts from changing provider propensity, this study aimed to decompose the compositional and behavioral drivers of the Caesarean section surge in Bangladesh between 2012 and 2025. MethodsNationally representative data were analyzed from the 2012-2013, 2019, and 2024-2025 Bangladesh Multiple Indicator Cluster Surveys (MICS), comprising 26,534 women aged 15-49 years who delivered a child within the preceding two years. Survey skip-logic was harmonized to retain unmedicalized cohorts receiving zero antenatal care (ANC). A survey-weighted multivariate Linear Probability Model (LPM) Oaxaca-Blinder decomposition was applied to a complete-case cohort (N=16,179) to partition the prevalence change into population-level compositional shifts (endowments) and behavioral changes (coefficients). ResultsNational Caesarean section prevalence surged by 32.47 percentage points, rising from 19.48% in 2012 to 36.05% in 2019 and 51.95% in 2025 (p<0.001). Surgical delivery multiplied over sixfold among the poorest wealth quintile (5.53% to 34.37%), rose by 34.83 percentage points among rural mothers (15.66% to 50.49%), and reached 85.12% within private facilities. Multivariate decomposition demonstrated that 87.77% of the overall increase was attributable to compositional shifts rather than behavioral factors (12.23%). The sharp reduction in pregnancies receiving zero ANC visits (35.52% to 8.12%) independently drove 49.04% of the surge, while increased utilization of private clinics and NGOs (18.20% to 54.36%) explained 43.39%. Conversely, biological indications such as fetal macrosomia contributed less than 1%. ConclusionsThe unprecedented escalation of Caesarean sections in Bangladesh represents a profound pattern of systemic over-medicalization that is independent of baseline clinical risk. The surge is overwhelmingly structural, driven by the disproportionate concentration of deliveries within the commercialized private healthcare sector and supplier-induced demand following integration into formal clinical pathways. Reversing this trajectory necessitates immediate regulatory intervention, specifically the mandate of clinical auditing frameworks such as the Robson classification, to decouple financial incentives from obstetric decision-making in private facilities.

papers.title: Objective sleep tracking for fatigue management in cargo pilots: six months of continuous smart-ring monitoring
papers.abstract: Aviation fatigue management estimates crew sleep from rosters and self-report. We examined how sleep duration changes around flights and with departure and landing times. In an observational cohort study, 13 cargo pilots wore an Ultrahuman smart ring for six months in 2026. We linked 1,504 sleep sessions to the flown schedule. Linear mixed-effects models compared each sleep session with the same pilots rest nights, with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Total sleep time was 48 min shorter on the night before a flight (95% CI 32 to 65 min) and 28 min shorter in the first sleep after one (95% CI 13 to 43 min). Later nights did not differ. Sleep duration varied with clock time. Compared with evening departures and landings, respectively, pilots slept 57 min less before a departure between 06:00h and 11:59h (95% CI 14 to 101 min) and 97 min less after a landing between 00:00h and 05:59h (95% CI 37 to 156 min). Flight direction and length showed no association. Differences between pilots explained 14.1% of the variance in total sleep time, more than six times the 2.2% explained by duty position. Fatigue risk management could plan rest around departure and landing times.

papers.title: "It Just Puts You Out!" Tranq Sleep, Sensory Discernment, and the Experience of Consuming Xylazine-Adulterated Fentanyl in Rural North Carolina
papers.abstract: BackgroundXylazine, a veterinary sedative not approved for human use, has emerged as a consequential adulterant in the U.S. illicit fentanyl supply. Although a growing body of qualitative research has documented the experiences of fentanyl consumers exposed to tranq in large Northeastern cities, little is known about how xylazine is experienced in rural or Southern regions where the evolution of the illicit drug supply often lags behind its urban equivalents. This study examines how fentanyl consumers in west-central North Carolina detect, comprehend and respond to the widespread adulteration of fentanyl markets with xylazine. MethodsBetween September and December of 2025, a seasoned interviewer conducted 25 in-depth, semi-structured qualitative interviews with fentanyl consumers recruited from both fixed and mobile syringe service programs in west-central North Carolina. Interviews explored sensory discernment strategies, pharmacologic effects, and behavioral responses to the presence of xylazine. Data were analyzed using a combined deductive-inductive thematic approach in QSR NVivo 14.0. ResultsParticipants described a distinctive repertoire of sensory strategies for identifying xylazine in their fentanyl supply, including the appearance of drug residue on foil, bitterness and chemical odor when smoked, and altered viscosity when injected. A minority described an inability to detect xylazine through sensory cues. Participants consistently distinguished a profound involuntary sedation they called "tranq sleep" from the familiar opioid nod, characterizing it by nearly instantaneous loss of consciousness with severe withdrawal upon awakening. While nearly all participants expressed strong aversion to xylazine, a meaningful minority valued its amplifying effects to improve a diminishing fentanyl high. ConclusionsThis study offers among the first qualitative description of xylazine exposure in a rural fentanyl market. Findings extend the xylazine literature geographically and pharmacologically and underscore the urgency of harm reduction responses tailored to the distinctive harms of xylazine. In particular, adverse health outcomes that accumulate during episodes of protracted and unarousable sedation, including physical injury, victimization, and the severe withdrawal syndrome that follows upon awakening. Highlightsxylazine; tranq sleep, fentanyl; qualitative methods; harm reduction; rural drug markets; drug discernment

papers.title: Enablers and barriers to scaling an ECD parenting program into primary health care services in rural Bangladesh
papers.abstract: Early childhood development programs play a crucial role in fostering child development. However, scaling-up these programs in low- and middle-income countries poses significant challenges. We conducted a mixed-method study of an evidence-based early childhood parenting program integrated into the primary health care services (community clinics) across four districts in rural Bangladesh. The program caters to caregivers of children aged 6-36 months with mild-to-moderate malnutrition. The parenting program is delivered by government community health workers (CHWs) with small groups of mother-child dyads within the community clinic setting as part of their routine duties. Mothers-child dyads attend fortnightly sessions for one year. CHWs are trained and monitored by government supervisors with overall oversight provided by government health staff at the sub-district and district level. The aim of the study was to identify the strengths and weaknesses of the program and strategies for improvement. Quantitative data included data from clinic logbooks, observations of session quality (n=60), and in-person interviews with participating mothers (n=185) in sixty clinics and phone interviews with mothers (n=164) in a further eighty clinics. Qualitative data included in-depth interviews with CHWs (n=20), government inspectors (n=16), and managers (n=4), and focus group discussions with mothers (n=4 groups, n=30 mothers), and grandmothers (n=4 groups, n=28 grandmothers) across twelve clinics. Results indicated that the key enablers to program implementation included strong government ownership, high compliance in implementing the program by CHWs, adequate session quality, satisfactory session attendance, and positive attitudes towards the program by all stakeholders. Key barriers included low levels of supervision, insufficient advocacy messaging within the community, poor communication across health staff at the different levels, and challenges in providing play materials at scale. The findings are being used to inform revisions to the program to enhance implementation fidelity and sustainability within the health system.

papers.title: Building a community-academic partnership in public housing: Lessons from applying the CBPR Partnership Readiness Model
papers.abstract: The DASH (Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension) eating plan has been shown to reduce hypertension; however, adherence is low among low-income African American (AA) women, who experience a disproportionate burden of hypertension. To better understand barriers to DASH among low-income AA women, specifically AA women living in public housing, we established a community-academic partnership using a project advisory board (PAB). This paper applies the CBPR Partnership Readiness Model to assess community stakeholder readiness for the partnership. PAB members were recruited through ongoing research and volunteer work in the target community. We developed a 33-page PAB workbook clarifying study goals, member roles and expectations, and hypertension information. A questionnaire was used to gather feedback on members experiences. PAB membership increased by 150% after the first year following a second recruitment phase. Members reported satisfaction with progress toward local food equity initiatives and with partnership sustainability. Findings indicate the model was helpful in evaluating the PAB formation process for a project involving public housing stakeholders. PABs can help build local support for community-engaged projects. When members can see the advantages of their involvement, partnerships are strengthened.

papers.title: Physician-reported practices regarding obesity management in patients aged under 60 years with osteoarthritis in Jordan: a cross-sectional survey
papers.abstract: BackgroundObesity is an important modifiable risk factor for the development and progression of osteoarthritis (OA), particularly in weight-bearing joints. However, limited information is available regarding physicians practices in addressing obesity among patients with OA in Jordan. This study assessed self-reported obesity-management practices among physicians caring for patients aged under 60 years with OA. MethodsWe conducted an anonymous, cross-sectional convenience survey between December 2021 and January 2022. Physicians from orthopaedics, family medicine, general internal medicine, and rheumatology were recruited through professional networks and social-media platforms. Participants worked in Ministry of Health, private, university, and military healthcare institutions in Jordan. The questionnaire assessed obesity-related counselling, weight or body mass index (BMI) monitoring, consultation time, and referral for weight-reduction interventions among patients aged under 60 years with obesity and OA. ResultsA total of 308 physicians completed the questionnaire. Of these, 162 (52.6%) were orthopedic specialists or trainees and 146 (47.4%) were from other specialties, including primary care, general internal medicine, rheumatology, and general surgery. A total of 138 (44.8%) respondents worked in Ministry of Health healthcare institutions, 87 (28.2%) worked in the private sector, and 83 (26.9%) worked in university or military institutions. Eighty-five respondents (27.6%) reported explaining the effect of obesity on weight-bearing joints to almost all patients with obesity and OA, whereas 149 (48.4%) did so for approximately half of their patients and 74 (24.0%) rarely or never did so. Only 26 respondents (8.4%) reported monitoring weight or BMI in almost all target patients, while 187 (60.7%) reported doing so rarely or in only a few patients. Referral for dietetic or other weight-reduction interventions was reported for almost all target patients by 31 respondents (10.1%), whereas 152 (49.4%) reported rarely or never making such referrals. The remaining respondents reported counselling, monitoring, or referral for approximately half of their target patients. ConclusionsAmong participating physicians in Jordan, obesity counselling, weight or BMI monitoring, and referral for weight-reduction interventions were inconsistently incorporated into the management of patients aged under 60 years with OA. These findings support the integration of routine weight assessment, structured obesity counselling, and accessible multidisciplinary referral pathways into OA care. Because this study used convenience sampling and self-reported data, the findings should not be assumed to represent all physicians practising in Jordan.

papers.title: The toll of an early bell? School start time and adolescent sleep quality in Flanders, Belgium
papers.abstract: Study objectivesAdolescent sleep deprivation is a major public health concern, with insufficient and poor-quality sleep associated with adverse physical, mental and cognitive outcomes. Early school start times may contribute to sleep restriction by conflicting with the biologically delayed sleep patterns that emerge during puberty. This study examined the effect of school start times on sleep duration and sleep quality among secondary school students. MethodsData were obtained from the 2022 Flemish Health Behaviour in School-aged Children (HBSC) study, including 12,329 adolescents from grade 1 to 6 in 94 secondary schools in Flanders. School start times were obtained from participating schools and sleep duration and sleep quality were assessed using self-report measures. Data were analyzed using traditional statistical methods (i.e., linear regression) and debiased machine learning methods (i.e., assumption lean regression, dose response curves and modified treatment policies). ResultsNo clinically meaningful effects of school start times on sleep outcomes were observed. In machine learning models, a 10-minute delay in start time was associated with non-significant changes in sleep quality (0.01 points on a 1-5 scale; 95% CI, -0.05 to 0.06) and school-day sleep duration (3.5 minutes; 95% CI, -1.0 to 8.0). ConclusionsWithin the narrow range of school start times observed in Flemish secondary schools, confidence intervals excluded clinically meaningful effects of later start times on adolescent sleep duration and sleep quality. Whether larger delays would improve sleep remains to be determined. Statement of significanceAdolescent sleep deprivation is a major public health concern, and delaying school start times has been widely advocated as a structural strategy to improve sleep. However, evidence remains largely observational, with varying approaches to confounding control, and European data are scarce. Using causal inference methods in a population-based sample of over 12,000 Flemish secondary school students, this study showed that differences in school start times within the range currently observed were unlikely to meaningfully improve sleep duration or sleep quality. These findings suggest that modest variations in start times may be insufficient to improve adolescent sleep, highlighting the need to evaluate whether substantially later start times, while accounting for factors like commuting time, are required to generate measurable sleep benefits.

papers.title: Risk Omission and Limited Disclosure in Dietary Supplement Promotion by Social Media Influencers
papers.abstract: ImportanceDietary supplements are commonly used by adolescents and can carry risks including adverse effects, drug interactions, and contamination-related harms. Social media influencers are prominent sources of health, fitness, and nutrition information for adolescents, yet little is known about how supplements are promoted in influencer environments relevant to young people or whether potential risks are communicated alongside claimed benefits. ObjectiveTo characterize dietary supplement promotion among Instagram influencers identified through audience-centered sampling in studies of adolescents, focusing on supplement types, advertising disclosure, persuasive strategies, and communication of benefits and harms. Design, Setting, and ParticipantsCross-sectional content analysis of 1120 dietary supplement presentations in 727 Instagram posts by 84 influencer accounts identified through 2 independent youth-focused studies in Switzerland and Austria. Main Outcomes and MeasuresMain outcomes were supplement types, overall tone, advertising disclosure, persuasive strategies, and communication of benefits and harms. Mixed-effects logistic regression models with random intercepts for influencer accounts examined associations of influencer characteristics and supplement categories with personal experience narratives and benefit claims. Outcomes with sparse distributions were summarized descriptively. ResultsOf 1120 supplement presentations, 1092 (97.5%) were promotional in tone and 1088 (97.1%) involved advertising, of which 802 (73.7%) lacked disclosure. Sports nutrition supplements accounted for 566 presentations (50.5%). Personal experience narratives were present in 458 presentations (40.9%), whereas evidence cues were present in only 42 (3.8%). Benefits were mentioned in 269 presentations (24.0%), approximately 10 times as often as harms (26 [2.3%]), and no presentation mentioned drug interactions or contamination risks. Conclusions and RelevanceAmong influencers identified through audience-centered sampling in studies of adolescents, dietary supplement promotion was highly commercialized, advertising was frequently undisclosed, and benefit communication substantially outweighed risk communication. The scarcity of harm communication and omission of clinically relevant risk information suggest that influencer environments relevant to adolescents may provide limited information for evaluating the potential risks of dietary supplements. Key PointsO_ST_ABSQuestionC_ST_ABSHow are dietary supplements promoted by social media influencers identified through youth-focused sampling, and to what extent do they communicate risks alongside claimed benefits? FindingsIn this cross-sectional content analysis of 1120 dietary supplement presentations across 727 Instagram posts by 84 influencers identified through 2 youth-focused studies, 97.1% involved advertising, of which 73.7% lacked disclosure. Benefits were mentioned approximately 10 times as often as harms, and no presentation mentioned drug interactions or contamination risks. MeaningDietary supplement promotion in influencer environments relevant to adolescents is highly commercialized, frequently undisclosed, and provides limited clinically relevant safety information.

papers.title: A statistical calibration framework for subnational health surveillance from routine data and survey audits
papers.abstract: In many low- and middle-income countries, where civil registration and vital statistics remain incomplete, decision makers rely on estimates derived from large international household surveys. Those surveys are rarely powered for frequent subnational estimates, and the contraction in international aid has made their future uncertain. Small area estimation has supplemented them with increasingly available routine health records and satellite imagery to improve their precision, but the survey estimate remains the response variable. We propose a statistical calibration framework that inverts the roles of the two data sources, whereby the routine records provide a biased baseline estimator continuously over time at the subnational level of interest, while a probability survey is used intermittently to audit and adjust for the selection bias of the direct register estimator. We develop the corresponding modelling and estimation methods, including diagnostic and analysis tools for the transport assumption that the out-of-survey subpopulations and time points require. The proposed framework is applied in four African countries to estimate undiagnosed HIV positivity by district and the selection bias by age and sex, and we explain how it applies to other health surveillance needs with similar data settings.

papers.title: Toward Standards for Responsible AI in Health Communication: A Dual Method Pre-Deployment Risk Evaluation Framework and Case Study
papers.abstract: ContextGenerative AI tools are increasingly being considered for use in public health research and practice, yet standardized frameworks for pre-deployment evaluation of the risks AI tools pose - across dimensions of platform safety, audience appropriateness, and user readiness - have not been established for health communication contexts. Program or PolicyWe developed and implemented a dual-method pre-deployment evaluation framework that combines adversarial red-teaming and structured user testing to assess the readiness of a health communication AI tool. The framework was applied to the Trusted Health Information Assistant (THIA), a retrieval-augmented generation chatbot designed by NORC at the University of Chicago for use in public health communication research. ImplementationThe framework was implemented sequentially, beginning with red-teaming to identify safety, audience appropriateness, and reliability concerns before engaging end users. Five independent testers completed 28 structured red-team prompts, after which identified issues were remediated and verified. User testing was subsequently conducted with six participants (e.g., caregivers of older adults) and included direct interaction with THIA, pre- and post-survey assessments, semi-structured interviews, and a review of backend analytics. EvaluationThe sequential, dual-method design successfully identified distinct categories of risk. Red-teaming identified platform integrity issues, including personally identifiable information (PII) handling and citation reliability. User testing subsequently assessed platform readiness under real-world conditions, surfacing trust dynamics and usability patterns. The convergence of findings across both methods validated the complementary design: each method identified distinct dimensions, together producing a more thorough and actionable assessment. DiscussionAs generative AI tools increasingly enter public health research and practice, ensuring that potential risks are systematically identified and addressed before they reach end users is paramount. Yet the field lacks shared standards for pre-deployment evaluation. AI developers rarely publish evaluation findings, leaving public health organizations with few replicable models to guide their own assessments. This report addresses that gap by documenting a structured, sequential framework including methods, instruments, scoring rubrics, and reporting structures for evaluating health communication AI tools prior to deployment.

papers.title: Hand sanitizer recalls during the COVID-19 pandemic: a descriptive analysis of regulatory records from Canada, Nepal, Singapore and the USA
papers.abstract: BackgroundAlcohol-based hand sanitizers were central to infection prevention during the COVID-19 pandemic. The abrupt rise in global demand fueled the emergence of substandard and unregulated products. Government regulatory bodies around the globe responded to this issue by tightening quality control and enforcing stringent limits on contaminants. This study aimed to descriptively analyze the reasons for, and timing of hand sanitizer recalls and safety warnings between 2020 and 2024. MethodologyWe extracted publicly available records from the national regulators of Canada, Nepal, Singapore, and the USA. The database was analyzed by country, year, and reason for recall to identify the recall patterns and regulatory practices. ResultsWe identified 1044 recalled products in Canada (277), Nepal (39), Singapore (26), and the USA (702). Major reasons for recall were administrative reasons such as non-compliance, non-response to the regulator, and unregistered or unauthorized sale (43.9%) followed by contamination with hazardous chemicals such as methanol, acetaldehyde, and benzene (37.4%) and subpotent ethanol or isopropanol (15.6%). Two-thirds of the recall records were from the USA followed by Canada, Nepal, and Singapore. While most of the recalls were announced during the first year of COVID-19, the recalls did not follow a temporal trend. ConclusionThe recall records showcased product hazard risks during the pandemic, highlighting its global impacts. The recalls in each of the four countries may have missed other substandard hand sanitizer products. This underlines the importance of strict monitoring and public awareness for product safety. The recall records discussed in this paper describe regulatory activity and should not be read as the prevalence of substandard hand sanitizers. Robust emergency regulatory frameworks, rapid analytical verification, and distributed yet strictly monitored certified production systems may help reduce public health risks due to hand sanitizers in the future.

papers.title: Laboratory evaluation of five rapid diagnostic tests for the serological diagnosis of chronic Trypanosoma cruzi infection in Yucatan, Mexico
papers.abstract: Chagas disease (CD), caused by Trypanosoma cruzi, is a significant public health challenge in Latin America, where an estimated 70% of infected individuals remain undiagnosed. Rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs) offer a promising solution for new screening strategies, yet their performance has not been systematically assessed in Mexican cohorts. Here, we evaluated the diagnostic performance of five RDTs: Chagas Rapid Test (Certum), Bio-Chagas Rapid Test (Mexlab), BiolineTM Chagas Ab (Abbott), Chagas Rapid Test (Amunet) and Chagas Sero K-SeT (Coris BioConcept). Performance was tested using 79 archived human serum samples from Yucatan. All tests were benchmarked against the diagnostic reference algorithm established by the Mexican Official Norm (NOM), where samples were characterised as positive if they were reactive to [≥] 2 conventional serological assays (Chagatest Lisado, Chagatest Recombinante v4.0 and Chagatest HAI). The RDTs demonstrated variable diagnostic sensitivity. The BiolineTM Chagas Ab test demonstrated the highest sensitivity (97.2%, 95% CI: 85.5 - 99.9; 35/36 positive samples detected) and almost perfect statistical agreement with the NOM reference algorithm ({kappa}= 0.90; p < 0.0001). Similarly, the Chagas Sero K-SeT prototype showed a high sensitivity (91.7%, 95% CI: 77.5 - 98.2; 33/36 positive samples detected) and substantial concordance ({kappa}= 0.87, p < 0.0001) with the NOM-based composite result. In contrast, the remaining RDTs demonstrated low sensitivities (Certum: 0.0%, 95% CI: 0.0-9.7; Mexlab: 5.6%, 95% CI: 0.7-18.7; Amunet: 33.3%, 95% CI: 18.6-51.0), limiting their suitability for CD diagnostic algorithms, at least in Yucatan. Specificity was consistently high across the RDTs, ranging from 93.0% to 100% (95% CIs: 80.9-100). These findings underscore the need to locally validate diagnostic tools. The BiolineTM Chagas Ab and Chagas Sero K-SeT tests met the WHO benchmarks for RDT performance and, if validated in larger cohorts, could strengthen the screening of T. cruzi infection and epidemiological surveillance in Mexico. Author summaryChagas disease, caused by the parasite Trypanosoma cruzi, remains underdiagnosed in Mexico. Rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs) could help expand access to screening, particularly in settings where laboratory testing is difficult to implement. However, the performance of these tests can vary geographically and has not been systematically evaluated in Mexico. We evaluated four commercially available RDTs and one developmental prototype using archived serum samples from Yucatan, a region where Chagas disease is endemic. Results were compared with the diagnostic algorithm recommended by the Mexican Official Norm. The Bioline Chagas Ab test showed the highest sensitivity, detecting 35 of 36 positive samples, while the Chagas Sero K-SeT prototype detected 33. The other three commercial RDTs showed substantially lower sensitivity, detecting between 0 and 12 positive samples. Specificity was high across all five tests, ranging from 93.0% to 100%, indicating that most negative samples were correctly identified. However, the low sensitivity of three tests limits their usefulness for Chagas disease screening in Yucatan. Our findings highlight the importance of locally validating RDTs before their implementation. The BiolineTM Chagas Ab and Chagas Sero K-SeT tests show promise for Chagas disease screening in Mexico but require further evaluation using larger and geographically diverse cohorts.

papers.title: Household cooking fuels, symptoms compatible with pneumonia and inequalities in care seeking among children under five in the Republic of the Congo: a nationally representative survey analysis
papers.abstract: ObjectivesTo examine the association between household cooking fuels and symptoms compatible with pneumonia, and socioeconomic inequalities in care seeking, among children under five in the Republic of the Congo. MethodsSecondary analysis of the 2014-2015 Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey, the most recent national survey with available microdata on respiratory symptoms (9,159 children aged 0- 59 months), using survey-weighted logistic regression. ResultsThe weighted prevalence of caretaker-reported cough with fast or difficult breathing due to a chest problem was 5.9% (95% CI 5.3-6.6). Compared with electricity or gas, cooking with solid fuels (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.23, 1.34-3.73) or kerosene (aOR 2.63, 1.38-5.01) was associated with higher odds of symptoms, independently of wealth, education and residence (E- values 3.9 and 4.7). Only 28.2% (23.1-33.9) of children with symptoms were taken to a health facility or provider, from 17.8% in the poorest to 61.1% in the richest quintile (aOR 4.10, 1.96- 8.57 for the three richest versus the two poorest quintiles). ConclusionsPoorer Congolese children combine greater exposure to polluting cooking fuels and less access to care. Clean cooking policies should be combined with removal of financial barriers to care for sick children.
